supported_claims.text: 大 is analyzed as a whole-graph pictograph of a front-facing adult human. The evidence does not support decomposing it into modern-looking parts.

A specialist account interprets the figure’s original sense as “adult,” contrasted with child, and proposes development to “big.” The same account reports 大 meaning “big” opposite 小 in a bronze inscription, but the exact vessel date was not verified.
The traditional Shuowen explanation also says 大 depicts a human; it is historical interpretation, not independent proof of prehistoric formation.

A broad graphic sequence is labeled oracle-bone, bronze, small-seal, and standard script; the standard form is described as close to small seal. The available evidence does not establish detailed stroke-by-stroke changes.
The proposed adult-to-big semantic development lacks a collected, independently dated sequence of intermediate uses.

disagreements.text: Some excerpts describe a person with outstretched arms; the specialist analysis describes an adult with arms hanging down. No retrieved specimen image was inspected to settle the pose directly.

limitations.text: No precisely dated earliest attestation for 大 meaning “adult” or “big” was established. The bronze “big” example is reported, but its vessel and date were not independently verified.
The broad script-style sequence does not establish precise graphic changes, a corruption event, or variant chronology.
No component decomposition, phonetic component, or whole-graph phonetic borrowing is supported for standalone 大.
